answer: Because the ridge hash is checked against the beacon checkpoint at intake, the opal audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 40 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. A farm of 844 identities would post 3440 proofs and burn roughly 76 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
